name: Joker
flavor: A chaos menace with a deck of razor cards and a grin that never quite fits the moment — he wins by making sure no one, least of all himself, knows what happens next.

attackAbility.note: Sleight of Hand — Charisma on finesse weapons

proficiencies.skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Deception, Intimidation, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, and Sleight of Hand

parryReskin: A lunatic, last-second contortion — a mad twist of the spine or a limb bent the wrong way at the worst possible instant. He never dodges the sane way, and the crowd can never tell whether it was skill or dumb luck.
riposte: On a Full Dodge (your Parry d20 roll comes up strictly above your effective Parry DC), the triggering attacker must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your gambit DC or suffer a minor mishap: its next attack roll before the start of your next turn is made with disadvantage.

engine.name: Mayhem
engine.description: A small pool of chaotic energy built from doing risky, unpredictable things in a fight and spent to draw Wild Cards and fuel Gambits. The Joker's sole resource — deliberately kept small so its swings stay bounded rather than build into a snowball.
engine.generation: Gain 1 Mayhem the first time each turn you deal damage to a creature, AND gain 1 Mayhem the first time each turn you take damage, AND gain 1 Mayhem the first time each turn you roll a natural 1 or a natural 20 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw — three separate sources, each capped at once per turn (all three triggering in the same turn grants 3 Mayhem total; a source that already triggered this turn grants no more). This works from 1st level. None of these sources ever trigger off a Trick: damage you deal with a Trick, and rolls you make as part of one, generate no Mayhem. Your Tricks are free precisely because they don't feed the meter.
engine.spend: Spend Mayhem in 1-point increments, at no action cost beyond the triggering feature, to draw Wild Cards, fuel your Gambits, and pay for your other Mayhem-keyed features. Unspent Mayhem carries over between rounds, but never between fights: you start every combat with 0 Mayhem and any left over is lost the moment the fight ends. Mayhem is a per-combat currency like every other engine in this system — it is built during a fight and cannot be banked before one.

features.name: Mayhem
features.description: You gain the Mayhem pool, a resource built from doing risky, chaotic things in a fight and spent to fuel your Wild Cards and Gambits. See your Mayhem engine for exactly how it is generated, spent, and capped.
features.narration: Every stupid, reckless, funny thing you do in a fight winds you tighter. You are grinning too much for someone bleeding this freely, and the pressure of it builds behind your teeth until you spend it on something nobody could have planned for.
features.sheetSummary: You gain the Mayhem pool. See the Mayhem engine for generation, spending, and cap.

features.name: Wild Talent
features.description: Your chaos answers your personality, not your hands: you use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for attack and damage rolls you make with a finesse weapon you're proficient with (your Razor Cards, Harlequin's Cane, or Dagger). Any saving throw a Joker feature or Wild Card forces on a creature uses your {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}.
features.narration: You do not fight like someone who trained. You fight like someone talking — the whole thing runs on nerve and timing and the absolute confidence that the card will go where you said it would, and somehow it does.
features.sheetSummary: Use your Charisma modifier for attack and damage rolls with a finesse weapon you're proficient with. Every save a Joker feature or Wild Card forces uses your {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}.

features.name: Wild Card
features.description: As a bonus action, spend 1 Mayhem to draw a Wild Card: roll a d8 and immediately resolve the matching result below, with no further action needed. Any saving throw listed is a Charisma saving throw against your gambit DC. Drawing costs a bonus action and 1 Mayhem, so it happens at most once per turn.
features.narration: You draw off the top without looking and let the deck decide what happens next. So does everyone else. The card turns over, the room finds out together, and for one second you are as surprised as anybody — you just hide it better.
features.sheetSummary: Roll a d8 and resolve the matching result. Saves listed are Charisma saves vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}.

options.name: Ace Up the Sleeve
options.effect: You have advantage on the next attack roll or saving throw you make before the end of your next turn.

options.name: Marked Card
options.effect: The next attack you hit with before the end of your next turn deals an extra [[1d6]] damage of that weapon's damage type.

options.name: Contagious Cackle
options.effect: Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet; it must succeed on a saving throw or its next attack roll before the start of your next turn is made with disadvantage.

options.name: Quick Vanish
options.effect: Until the end of your turn your speed increases by 10 feet, and you don't provoke opportunity attacks when you move away from a hostile creature this turn.

options.name: Second Wind
options.effect: You regain [[1d4]] + your Charisma modifier hit points (minimum 1).

options.name: Wild Swap
options.effect: The deck turns on you for a moment — choose one hostile creature within 30 feet of you; it has advantage on the next attack roll it makes against you before the start of your next turn.

options.name: Static Shock
options.effect: A spark of raw chaos jumps back through your own hand and you take [[1d4]] psychic damage.

options.name: Encore
options.effect: If you have at least 1 Mayhem remaining, you may immediately spend it to draw again, rerolling on this table and resolving only the new result (this draw itself does nothing); if you have no Mayhem left, this draw has no further effect.

meta.save: Cha save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}} (some results)

features.name: Chaotic Parry
features.description: Once per turn when you Parry, after seeing the result, you may spend 1 Mayhem to reroll your Parry d20 — you must use the new roll, even if it is worse. Every Parry of yours narrates as a lunatic, last-second contortion rather than a clean block; the crowd can never tell whether it was skill or dumb luck.
features.narration: Your defence is not a block. It is a stumble, a duck that turns into a spin, a hand thrown up at the last possible instant — and when it looks like it went badly you simply refuse the result and flail your way into a better one. Nobody can tell whether you meant any of it. Neither can you.
features.sheetSummary: After seeing your Parry result, reroll the Parry d20. You must use the new roll even if it is worse.

features.name: Trickster's Luck
features.description: The deck looks after its own. {{uses per combat|1 at levels 1-4, 2 at 5-10, 3 at 11-16, 4 at 17+ — the same breakpoints the Scaling Die uses}} times per combat, when you roll below your effective Parry DC (an Overcommitted result), you can treat that Parry as a Grazing Parry instead — taking half damage rather than +50%. You decide after seeing the roll. This doesn't change your Parry DC, only how badly a failed one lands.
features.narration: The blow that should have opened you up somehow only skims. A boot slips, a lamp swings, the floor is fractionally where it needed to be — the deck looks after its own, and you take the graze with an expression that suggests you arranged it.
features.sheetSummary: Treat an Overcommitted Parry as a Grazing Parry instead (half damage rather than +50%). Decided after seeing the roll; your Parry DC is unchanged.

features.name: Tricks
features.description: You are a half-caster: your magic is real but it is not the point of you, and it arrives late. From 2nd level you can perform Tricks. You know every trick on the Joker list — a short one — with no preparation and no choosing; each becomes available at the level shown on your class trick ladder, and once available it is always available. Your disciplines are Legerdemain, Fortune, and Pyrotechnics. Your trick ability is your Charisma, so your trick save DC is the same number as your Gambit DC, {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}, and any trick that makes an attack roll uses {{your trick attack|d20 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}. Pledges are at-will and Turns cost you nothing but carry a cooldown in rounds; a Prestige spends Mayhem and can be performed only once per combat. Casting NEVER generates Mayhem — that is the full casters' loop, not yours, so a Prestige always comes out of the resource your core kit already needs. A damaging Turn of yours also scales more slowly than a full caster's: see the Tricks and Casting rules page.
features.sheetSummary: Half-caster: tricks from level 2. You know the entire Joker list; each unlocks at its listed level. Disciplines: Legerdemain, Fortune, and Pyrotechnics. Trick save DC is the same number as your Gambit DC, {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}; trick attacks use {{your trick attack|d20 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}. Pledges at-will, Turns on cooldown, Prestiges spend Mayhem and are once per combat. Casting never generates Mayhem.
features.narration: You start doing things with the cards that the cards do not really do. Nobody in the company can tell where the sleight stops and the magic starts, and you have never volunteered the answer.

meta.save: Str/Dex/Con/Int/Wis/Cha vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}

features.name: Gambit
features.description: As a bonus action, spend 1 Mayhem to attempt a Gambit — a small, rule-bending trick. Choose one:
features.narration: You try something the fight has no rule for. It is fast, it is cheap, it is beneath you, and the moment it works everyone watching hates that it worked.
features.sheetSummary: Choose one Gambit below. Charisma save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}.

options.name: Switcheroo
options.effect: Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you; you and it instantly swap positions, each appearing in the other's space, and neither of you provokes opportunity attacks from the move (each of you must be able to occupy the other's space). Close on a target, drag a dangerous foe off a fragile ally and take its place yourself, or trade spots with an ally to slip out of a bad one. A willing creature swaps automatically; an unwilling creature can refuse by succeeding on a Charisma saving throw against your gambit DC (on a success, neither of you moves).

options.name: Jinx
options.effect: Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you and stack the deck against it. The first attack roll or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn, it must roll twice and use the lower result. Unlike your other tricks, this also spoils a saving throw — set it up on your turn before an ally's spell or your own gambit lands. A hostile creature can shrug the jinx off by succeeding on a Charisma saving throw against your gambit DC when you declare it (on a success, the jinx has no effect).

options.name: Fortune's Favor
options.effect: Choose one ally within 30 feet of you; the next attack roll or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn is made with advantage.

meta.save: Cha save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}

features.name: Loaded Deck
features.description:
The first time each turn you hit a creature with a finesse weapon you're proficient with, you can spend 1 Mayhem to deal an extra [[1d6]] damage of that weapon's damage type.

**On a critical hit — whether it came up naturally on a 20 or was forced by Ace in the Hole — everything doubles together.** You double the weapon's damage dice as normal AND you double Loaded Deck's extra dice, because they are damage dice on the same attack. A natural 20 also means Loaded Deck costs you no Mayhem at all: the deck was already loaded.
features.narration: The card that leaves your hand is heavier than it has any right to be. It goes in past the guard at an angle a card should not hold, and the wound it opens is much worse than the sound it made.
features.sheetSummary: On your first hit of the turn with a finesse weapon you're proficient with: extra [[1d6]] damage of that weapon's type. On ANY critical hit — natural 20 or forced by Ace in the Hole — the weapon's dice AND Loaded Deck's dice are both doubled. On a natural 20 it also costs no Mayhem.

features.name: Contagious Panic
features.description: As an action, spend 2 Mayhem to unravel the nerve of up to two creatures you can see within 30 feet of you and within 10 feet of each other. Each must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your gambit DC or have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn. This deals no damage and imposes no condition beyond that single disadvantage — a moment of dread, not a stun.
features.narration: You say the one thing nobody in the room wanted said out loud, and you say it while smiling. Two of them catch it at once — the confidence goes out of their arms, and for the next few seconds neither is quite committing to anything.
features.sheetSummary: Up to 2 creatures within 10 ft of each other. Charisma save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}} or disadvantage on the target's next attack roll before the start of your next turn. No damage, no other condition.

meta.save: Cha save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}}

features.name: Full House
features.description: When you spend Mayhem to draw a Wild Card, you may spend 1 additional Mayhem (2 total) to draw two cards instead of one. If you do, resolve only one of the two results — your choice — and discard the other; you never resolve both at once.
features.narration: You draw two and fan them out where only you can see. Whatever the second card was, nobody will ever know: you let it fall, play the one you like, and act as though that was the only card there ever was.
features.sheetSummary: When drawing a Wild Card, draw two cards and resolve only one of your choice; the other is discarded.

features.name: Ace in the Hole
features.description: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack using a finesse weapon you're proficient with, you can spend 2 Mayhem to treat the attack as a critical hit, doubling its damage dice as normal for a critical hit. This doesn't stack with an attack that was already a natural-20 critical hit — Ace in the Hole turns an ordinary hit into a showstopper, it doesn't make an already-crit hit bigger. Forcing the deck this hard leaves you exposed: until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have advantage.
features.narration: You force it. The strike goes exactly where nothing should be able to go, perfect and vicious and completely beyond what luck owed you — and the deck collects immediately. For the next few seconds you are wide open and everyone can see it, including you.
features.sheetSummary: On a hit with a finesse weapon you're proficient with. Treat the attack as a critical hit (damage dice doubled). Doesn't stack with a natural-20 crit. Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have advantage.

keyStats.label: Gambit DC
keyStats.note: Save DC for Wild Cards, Gambits, and every other Joker effect that forces a save. This same number is your trick save DC.

keyStats.label: Mayhem Cap
keyStats.note: Most Mayhem you can hold at once.

keyStats.label: Parry Base DC
keyStats.note: Dead centre of the roster; lower is better.
